title: Predicting Consequences and Reinforcing Navigation Policies with Latent World Models
abstract: arXiv:2608.26190v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: World models enable agents to reason about future outcomes and learn policies from their knowledge of state transition, but existing approaches primarily focus on reconstructing future observations or features, which introduces unnecessary complexity and limits their effectiveness for decision making. In this work, we propose a compatibility prediction Latent World Model (LWM) for robot navigation that predicts action-conditioned latent feature compatibility rather than reconstructing observations. translated_title: 预测后果与利用潜在世界模型强化导航策略
translated_abstract: 世界模型使智能体能够推理未来结果，并从其对状态转移的知识中学习策略，但现有方法主要侧重于重建未来观测或特征，这引入了不必要的复杂性并限制了其在决策中的有效性。在这项工作中，我们提出了一种用于机器人导航的兼容性预测潜在世界模型（LWM），该模型预测动作条件下的潜在特征兼容性，而非重建观测。我们的关键洞察是，空间邻近性与潜在特征相似性相关，从而使得动作后果可以直接在潜在空间中进行评估。为了支持反事实训练，我们的模型利用跨轨迹采样的动作序列，并学习预测哪些序列更接近目标。此外，我们展示了所学世界模型如何从未标记的视频数据中监督策略学习，并进一步改进导航性能。
tldr: 本文提出一种潜在世界模型，通过预测动作条件下的潜在特征兼容性而非重建观测，直接评估动作后果，并利用反事实训练从无标签视频中学习导航策略。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a latent world model that predicts action-conditioned latent feature compatibility instead of reconstructing observations, directly evaluating action consequences and enabling navigation policy learning from unlabeled video via counterfactual training.
